recommendation_2: Add a nn.Dropout(0.2) layer between the fc1 and fc layers in the existing Net class.
rationale_2: With high label skew (e.g., Client 0 dominated by class 5), the model is prone to overfitting the majority class on local clients; dropout provides necessary regularization to improve global generalization in Federated Learning.
recommendation_3: Replace the F.relu activation in the forward method with F.leaky_relu(x, negative_slope=0.01) or F.elu(x).
rationale_3: ReLU can suffer from 'dying neurons' where gradients become zero; Leaky ReLU or ELU ensures that neurons continue to learn even for negative inputs, which helps stability during the divergent local updates typical of Non-IID data.
recommendation_4: Increase the depth of the MLP by adding a second hidden layer: nn.Linear(mid_dim, mid_dim) between fc1 and fc, with a total mid_dim of 256.
rationale_4: The current model is very shallow (one hidden layer). A deeper architecture with increased capacity can better model the complex decision boundaries required to separate 10 classes when training data is unevenly distributed.
recommendation_5: Replace the SGD optimizer in the train function with torch.optim.Adam(net.parameters(), lr=lr).
rationale_5: Adam uses adaptive learning rates for each parameter, which is generally more robust than standard SGD when dealing with the noisy gradients produced by highly skewed local datasets in a Federated environment.
